reconcile.connective: Gill reads one name for one office: Judas left eleven, Thomas's absence left ten in the room, but 'the twelve' remained their original title.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible presents ten (John 20:24), eleven (the Synoptics), and twelve (1 Corinthians 15:5) as three incompatible answers to one question.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "How many disciples did Jesus appear to in his first post resurrection appearance?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/eleven.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (online; contra/eleven.html)

excerpts.excerpt_text: …though there were then but eleven of them, Judas being gone from them, and having destroyed himself; and at the first appearance of Christ to them, there were but ten present, Thomas being absent; and yet because their original number, when first chosen and called, were twelve, they still went by the same name; see Joh 20:24.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly reconciles all three counts named in the question in one sentence: ten present at the first appearance (John 20:24), eleven once Judas was gone, and 'the twelve' as the apostles' retained original title — the single strongest available harmonization.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on 1 Corinthians 15:5
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this exact tension directly, reconciling the ten present at the first appearance (John 20:24) and the eleven left after Judas's death with Paul's 'the twelve' by reading it as the apostles' retained original title, not a headcount (used as this row's reconcile excerpt). John Haley's Alleged Discrepancies was checked via full-text search of the archive.org djvu transcript for 'twelve', 'eleven', 'Cephas', 'Corinthians xv', and 'Matthias' and does not treat this passage, so Gill is used per the contract's fallback clause.
